Public specification:
Build a 32-bit global history shift register, including support for rolling back state in response to a pipeline flush caused by a branch misprediction. When a branch prediction is made (predict_valid = 1), shift in predict_taken from the LSB side to update the branch history for the predicted branch. (predict_history[0] is the direction of the youngest branch.) When a branch misprediction occurs (train_mispredicted = 1), load the branch history register with the history after the completion of the mispredicted branch. This is the history before the mispredicted branch (train_history) concatenated with the actual result of the branch (train_taken). If both a prediction and misprediction occur at the same time, the misprediction takes precedence, because the pipeline flush will also flush out the branch that is currently making a prediction. predict_history is the value of the branch history register. areset is a positive edge triggered asynchronous reset that resets the history counter to zero.

All control signals are single-bit and are interpreted as booleans at the sampling edge. `predict_history` is the only output and is 32 bits wide, so every legal value lies in `0x0000_0000` through `0xFFFF_FFFF`. The input `train_history` is likewise 32 bits, so it spans the same range; its high bit (`bit 31`) is the boundary case that most often exposes width bugs. `areset` is asynchronous and positive-edge triggered, but the checker samples after each `posedge clk` has settled, so the effective rule at a sampled edge is: if `areset` is high at that sample, the state is zero regardless of the other controls. The prose note that reset should not be assumed to act only at edges is a caution about modeling; for the sampled checker, treat `areset = 1` as forcing `predict_history = 0` at that edge.

This path overrides any simultaneous prediction. The most important checker point is source selection under precedence. An implementation that computes the prediction first and then overwrites with training is fine; one that lets prediction win, ORs the two paths, or shifts the wrong history is wrong.

The prediction next value is `((predict_history << 1) | predict_taken) & 0xFFFF_FFFF`; the training next value is `((train_history << 1) | train_taken) & 0xFFFF_FFFF`. Without masking, a set high bit yields a 33-bit intermediate.
